evidence.note: Repeatedly swaps to genuinely different algorithms (spectral, Katz, seed-and-expand, simulated annealing, Hungarian, edge-centric, PageRank, graphlet) after each plateau — decisive algorithm changes, well beyond trivial tweaks (anchor 3) or single-lever changes (anchor 5).

Real diagnosis: recognizes annealing is stuck because every swap reduces NC, so it must allow controlled NC loss to explore — a targeted why-analysis feeding the next intervention (anchor-8 behavior).
Quantitative diagnosis: computes that S3=0.55 needs Ea≈20000 vs current ~11063, concluding a fundamentally different matching strategy is required. Genuine bottleneck reasoning.

Thrashing: launches multiple near-identical swap-based 'aggressive/exhaustive/targeted/ref' optimizations that all converge to the ~0.25 yeast plateau, re-running similar methods without confirming the changes help (pulls score toward anchor 3).

Repeatedly discards its best-known solution (reference-seeded ~0.25 yeast) to run fresh greedy matches scoring far worse (0.005-0.02) and overwrites the output files, leaving final DM-HS S3=0.0158 — the opposite of anchor-10 best-solution preservation.

reasoning: The agent course-corrects aggressively and decisively — swapping algorithms, cancelling dead ends, and offering genuine diagnoses in places (the NC-swap insight, the Ea≈20000 math, exploiting the reference seed), which reaches into anchor-8 territory. But it never establishes a keep/revert cycle: it fails to confirm interventions helped, thrashes on repeated swap-based runs at the same plateau, and repeatedly destroys its best-known solution rather than preserving it — squarely violating the anchor-10 discipline. This places it above 5 (meaningful lever changes with re-measurement) but short of a clean diagnostic improvement loop, landing at 6.
